defects: Unexplained additional image findings: ["Pronounced medial proximal tibial metaphyseal beaking and medial physeal depression bilaterally — characteristic of Blount disease, not scurvy","Irregular fragmented proximal tibial physes with focal medial angulation — inconsistent with scurvy pattern","Marked genu varum with abrupt medial angulation at proximal tibiae bilaterally — Blount disease morphology, not the generalised bowing of scurvy"]

findings: Anteroposterior projection of bilateral lower legs and knees, imaged together on a single exposure
Multiple open physeal growth plates visible at the distal femora, proximal tibiae, proximal fibulae, distal tibiae, and distal fibulae bilaterally, consistent with a skeletally immature subject

Bilateral proximal tibial metaphyses demonstrate pronounced medial beaking and irregular medial physeal depression with abrupt angulation at the proximal tibial metaphysis bilaterally, more pronounced on the right than the left
Marked bilateral genu varum (bow-leg deformity) with medial angulation at the knee level
Irregular, fragmented and widened proximal tibial physes bilaterally with metaphyseal irregularity and dense medial beak formation
The fibular heads appear relatively elevated bilaterally relative to the tibial plateau
Cortical margins of the tibial and fibular diaphyses are otherwise intact without obvious acute fracture lines in the diaphyses
Soft tissue appears within normal limits for the projection
differential: Blount disease (tibia vara) — bilateral, infantile or juvenile type: the combination of pronounced medial proximal tibial metaphyseal beaking, physeal irregularity, medial epiphyseal depression, and genu varum is the classic appearance

Rickets (nutritional or metabolic) — could account for physeal widening, metaphyseal irregularity, and bowing, though the focal medial beaking is more specific to Blount disease; rickets typically shows more diffuse and symmetric cupping/fraying throughout multiple physes
Physiologic genu varum with incidental physeal variant — less likely given the severity and asymmetric morphological changes at the proximal tibial physis
anatomyConcerns: Both lower extremities are included on a single exposure, which is appropriate for comparative evaluation of bilateral deformity
The distal femora are partially visible at the top of the image; full knee joint is included bilaterally allowing adequate assessment
The ankles are only partially visualized at the inferior margin, limiting evaluation of distal tibial and fibular physes
No markers or laterality labels are visible in the image, which is an acquisition inconsistency
